vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: huo15-img-prompt
Version: 2.5.0

The bundle is a comprehensive and well-structured suite of tools for AI-driven image and video prompt engineering, featuring automated iteration, vision-based quality review, and multi-backend rendering. The scripts (e.g., auto_iterate.py, render_prompt.py, and claude_polish.py) interact with numerous legitimate AI service providers such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Replicate, and Fal using standard Python libraries (urllib). While the suite requires access to multiple sensitive API keys via environment variables, the code demonstrates that these keys are only transmitted to the official API endpoints for their intended purposes. No evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or malicious prompt injection was found; the file system access is limited to standard session persistence and image output.

llm.summary: The skill's scripts broadly match an image-prompt/iteration tool, but they call multiple external APIs and expect several API keys (Anthropic, DALL‑E/Replicate/Fal/other backends) and persist session files — yet the package/registry metadata did not declare any required credentials, which is an incoherent and potentially risky mismatch.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (prompt enhancement, review, auto-iterate) align with the provided scripts: enhance_prompt.py, image_review.py, auto_iterate.py, render_prompt.py, etc. The code implements the advertised features (preset mapping, A/B variants, Claude-based polish/revision, multiple backends). However, the skill's registry metadata lists no required environment variables or credentials, while the code clearly uses many service keys — this mismatch is notable.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the included scripts instruct network calls to external services (Anthropic/Claude endpoints, multiple image backends such as Replicate/Fal/jimeng/kling/hailuo/DALL‑E), persist sessions under ~/.huo15, and write render outputs. The runtime instructions and code also perform JSON parsing of remote responses and may send prompt + review context to external LLM/VLM APIs. These actions go beyond purely local prompt formatting and will transmit user input and generated prompts/images to third parties.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only install), which keeps risk lower than arbitrary downloads. However, the skill bundle includes multiple executable Python scripts that will be run when invoked — meaning code in the package will execute locally. There is no external binary download, but packaged code with network behavior is present and should be reviewed before running.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Multiple scripts expect API keys and environment variables (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, REPLICATE_API_TOKEN, FAL_KEY, ARK_API_KEY (jimeng), KLING_API_KEY, MINIMAX_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY etc.) though the registry metadata declared none. Requiring several unrelated service keys (anthropic + many image backends) is explainable by the advertised multi-backend functionality, but the omission from metadata is an incoherence and increases risk: the skill will attempt to read secrets from the environment if present.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The scripts persist sessions under ~/.huo15/sessions and save render outputs to disk. They do not request 'always: true' or attempt to change other skills' configs, but they do store full traces (subject + recipe + render path + review + revisions). This is expected for session & iteration features but can leak sensitive prompt content or metadata if not acceptable to the user.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill implements a substantial prompt-engineering and closed-loop image workflow that contacts external services (Anthropic/Claude and many image backends), saves session history in ~/.huo15, and will read API keys from your environment if present — but the published metadata did not list any required credentials. Before installing or running: 1) inspect the included scripts (already provided) to confirm you understand which services will be contacted and what environment variables they read; 2) only set API keys you trust to be used by this tool (avoid exposing broad cloud credentials); 3) if you want to avoid network calls, run with dry-run/no-render modes or avoid features that require ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or backend keys; 4) be aware that prompts, images, and revision traces are written to ~/.huo15 and render output directories — delete or sandbox these if needed; 5) consider running the code in an isolated environment (container or VM) and review any environment-variable handling if you have sensitive tokens in your shell.
llm.findings:
[uses-anthropic-api] expected: Scripts call Anthropic (Claude) for polishing, review, and revision (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). This is consistent with the advertised 'Claude polish' and 'Claude Vision review' features, but the registry did not declare the requirement for this credential.
[calls-external-image-backends] expected: render_prompt and auto_iterate dispatch to many backends (replicate/fal/jimeng/kling/hailuo/dalle/sd-webui/comfyui). These network calls are expected by the '10 backends' feature, but they require multiple distinct API keys (also not declared).
[session-persistence-home-dir] expected: The skill persists session files under ~/.huo15/sessions. This is expected for the multi-turn/session features, but users should be aware that prompts, seeds, and iteration history are written to disk.
[uses-urllib-urlopen] expected: The code uses urllib/urlopen for HTTP requests to API endpoints. This is normal for custom API calls, but review is advised because network requests will transmit user-provided prompts and review context.
